slides.title: Alibaba Unveils Qwen Robot Suite for Embodied AI
slides.highlight: Alibaba has introduced the Qwen Robot Suite for embodied AI, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and AI-mediated learning.

slides.title: Evaluating Large Language Models Abilities for Addressee, Turn-change, and Next Speaker Prediction in Meetings
slides.highlight: This research evaluates LLMs and multimodal LLMs on addressee detection and speaker prediction, contributing to HyECHO's focus on addressee/listener modeling and team state perception.

card.one_liner: LLMs outperform humans and supervised models in next speaker prediction for multi-party meetings using conversational context.
card.key_idea: A unified framework evaluating addressee detection, turn-change, and next speaker prediction across supervised models, text-based LLMs, and multimodal LLMs (MM-LLMs).
card.evaluation: Evaluated on the AMI Meeting Corpus using accuracy and F1 scores; compared against supervised baselines and human subjects via a web-based interface.
card.limitation: MM-LLMs struggle to effectively leverage raw audio-visual signals, and human evaluation was conducted by non-native English speakers.

slides.title: Bidirectional Tutoring for Developmental Motor Learning in Robots: Co-Developed Interaction Dynamics Support Stable Learning
slides.tldr: BIDIRECTIONAL TUTORING FOR ROBOT MOTOR LEARNING
slides.highlight: This research demonstrates that bidirectional tutoring, where tutors and robots dynamically adapt to each other, fosters more consistent behavioral patterns and stable motor learning than unidirectional interaction. This is relevant to RwB's focus on AI-mediated embodied learning and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: Bidirectional tutoring improves robot motor learning by co-developing trajectories that preserve behavioral coherence and generalization.
card.key_idea: A FEP-based neural network (PV-RNN) with generative replay learns from interactive tutor interventions, creating consistent sensorimotor patterns compared to passive unidirectional demonstrations.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via a humanoid robot object manipulation task using success rates and training loss across human and AI tutoring settings.
card.limitation: The human-tutoring experiment served as a proof-of-concept with only one tutor, limiting the diversity of human interaction data.

slides.title: MuVAP: Multimodal Multiparty Voice Activity Projection for Turn-taking Prediction in the Wild
slides.highlight: MuVAP enables speaker-aware turn-taking predictions using a single camera and monaural audio, supporting HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and listener modeling in hybrid teams.

card.one_liner: MuVAP predicts multiparty turn-taking using a single camera and monaural audio via role-relative projection.
card.key_idea: Grounds acoustic voice activity projections in face tracks using Role-Relative Projection, mapping N-speaker interactions onto a fixed 'current vs. next' floor-holder state for scalability.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on the new 31-hour AVCC dataset using Shift-Hold (Macro-F1) and Next-Speaker Prediction (Accuracy) against MLP and random baselines; results show MuVAP outperforms baselines.
card.limitation: Performance is lower in 'active' prediction tasks compared to 'silent' ones and decreases as the number of speakers increases.

slides.title: Generating Natural and Expressive Robot Gestures through Iterative Reinforcement Learning with Human Feedback using LLMs
slides.highlight: This research uses ChatGPT and iterative reinforcement learning with human feedback to create more fluid and expressive co-speech gestures for the Pepper humanoid robot, advancing human-robot interaction. This is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: Iterative RLHF improves the expressiveness, relevance, and fluidity of LLM-generated co-speech gestures for humanoid robots.
card.key_idea: GPT-4 generates motion code from a primitive function library, refined through five iterations of offline Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) and online few-shot prompting based on human ratings.
card.evaluation: 250 participants rated 20 videos per iteration on a 5-point Likert scale. Results showed statistically significant improvements (p<0.001) by the final iteration.
card.limitation: Reliance on low-level primitives leads to reduced gesture diversity and a tendency toward conservative, repetitive patterns like head nodding.

slides.title: WaveSync: Constrained Wavefront Optimization for Synchronized Co-Speech Gestures in Humanoid Robots
slides.tldr: SYNCHRONIZED CO-SPEECH GESTURES FOR HUMANOID ROBOTS
slides.highlight: WaveSync uses a hybrid framework and wavefront optimization to align expressive gestures with speech while ensuring kinematic feasibility. This is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: WaveSync synchronizes humanoid robot gestures with speech emphasis while respecting strict physical kinematic constraints.
card.key_idea: An LLM generates a Semantic Importance Wave; Dynamic Movement Primitives shape trajectories, and a wavefront optimizer aligns gesture peaks to speech stress using duration compression and forward propagation.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via PyBullet simulations across five scenarios using objective metrics (HbS, Jerk) and subjective Likert ratings from 20 participants; outperformed three ablated baselines.
card.limitation: Relies on a fixed action library, limiting its ability to handle unconstrained dialogue; not yet tested on physical hardware.

slides.title: Fast When, Careful Who: Dual-Process Multiparty Turn-Taking with Diffusion Augmentation
slides.highlight: This work proposes a two-stage audio-only pipeline for multiparty turn-taking and next-speaker prediction, contributing to HyECHO's focus on diarization and listener modeling in hybrid team states.

card.one_liner: A dual-process audio pipeline for multiparty turn-taking using diffusion-based background augmentation to improve shift detection.
card.key_idea: A fast WavLM-based 'gate' proposes turn boundaries, while a slow ECAPA-TDNN 'verifier' confirms floor transfers (HOLD vs SHIFT) and predicts the next speaker.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on VoxConverse using precision, recall, F1, and MAE. Outperformed a ResCNN-Siamese baseline and a dyadic VAP benchmark in shift detection.
card.limitation: Performance is constrained by boundary coverage, particularly in heavily overlapped or fast-exchange segments where acoustic cues are ambiguous.

slides.title: Richtech Robotics launches livestream for ADAM AI-powered humanoid
slides.highlight: Richtech Robotics has launched a livestream for the ADAM AI-powered humanoid, offering insights into humanoid interaction relevant to RwB.

slides.title: Improving Medical Communication using Rubric-Guided Counterfactual Recommendations
slides.tldr: OPTIMIZING TELEMEDICINE COMMUNICATION VIA COUNTERFACTUAL RECOMMENDATIONS
slides.highlight: This work introduces an LM-guided pipeline to refine communication features like tone and personalization, supporting MIMIC's focus on LLM-based agent models for societal-scale human-AI interaction.

card.one_liner: An LM-guided pipeline recommends minimal, interpretable communication changes to increase positive patient feedback in telemedicine.
card.key_idea: Uses APO for feature discovery and refinement, trains a feedback estimator, and performs budget-constrained counterfactual search over ordinal semantic features to suggest low-effort communication improvements.
card.evaluation: Evaluated using temporal holdouts and independent auditor models (LR, EBM). Recommendations yielded a +6.41% mean gain in predicted positive feedback probability.
card.limitation: The evaluation was conducted offline and requires prospective validation in real-world deployment to measure actual impact on patient feedback.
